# ezghcloud_hosted_queue_cluster (Resource)

A managed Kafka or RabbitMQ cluster in a subnet of your VPC: one node, or three that survive the loss of any one. Clients connect over TLS with a username and password. It comes with the user app, whose password is in a Secret. Destroying it deletes the cluster, every object in it and its users' Secrets.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A single-node RabbitMQ cluster. mode = "replicated" runs three nodes; a single cluster grows to
# replicated in place.
resource "ezghcloud_hosted_queue_cluster" "example" {
  project_id       = ezghcloud_project.example.id
  name             = "tasks"
  engine           = "rabbitmq"
  engine_version   = "4.4"
  instance_type    = "gp-1.large"
  storage_size_gib = 20
  subnet_id        = ezghcloud_subnet.example.id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `engine` (String) kafka or rabbitmq. Changing it replaces the cluster.
- `engine_version` (String) Engine version, 4.3 or 4.4 on both engines. A newer version upgrades in place, one node at a time (one-way); an older one is refused at plan.
- `instance_type` (String) A gp-1, gs-1 or hp-1 instance type (hp-1 for a single node only). Changes in place, one node at a time.
- `name` (String) Cluster name. Changes in place.
- `project_id` (String) Project identifier. Changing it replaces the cluster.
- `storage_size_gib` (Number) Each node's storage in GiB, at least 10. Grows in place; shrinking is refused.
- `subnet_id` (String) Subnet (sbn_) the cluster is in. Changing it replaces the cluster.

### Optional

- `allowed_source_cidrs` (List of String) 1 to 20 IPv4 CIDRs allowed to connect. Left out at create, the VPC's ranges; removing it later keeps the current list.
- `deletion_protection` (Boolean) While true, the cluster can't be destroyed.
- `description` (String) Optional description; null clears it.
- `maintenance_window_utc` (String) Weekly maintenance window, ddd:HH:MM-ddd:HH:MM UTC.
- `mode` (String) single (one node) or replicated (three, surviving the loss of any one). single grows to replicated in place; replicated can't go back to single, so that change is refused at plan.
- `operation_timeout` (String) Maximum wait for each asynchronous operation, for example 60m.
- `plaintext_port` (Boolean) Also serve password authentication without TLS inside the VPC (Kafka 9092 SASL_PLAINTEXT, RabbitMQ 5672 AMQP), for apps that can't do TLS. Changes in place.
- `raise_app_topics` (Boolean) Kafka: when mode grows to replicated, also give every topic an app created three copies. Read only with that change; topics created through EZGH without a replication factor and Kafka's internal topics are raised either way.
- `settings` (Attributes) Kafka's cluster settings; null on RabbitMQ, which takes none. A setting left out keeps its current value. Changes in place. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--settings))
- `storage_iops` (Number) Each node's provisioned storage IOPS. Changes in place.
- `storage_throughput_mbps` (Number) Each node's provisioned storage throughput in MB/s. Changes in place.
- `tags` (Map of String) Resource tags.
- `unauthenticated_access` (Attributes) Kafka only: a TLS listener on 9091 with no client authentication, for apps that can't do SASL, reachable only from allowed_source_cidrs and firewall peers. Null on RabbitMQ. Changes in place. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--unauthenticated_access))

### Read-Only

- `broker_hostnames` (List of String) Kafka: the name each broker advertises, by broker index. Empty on RabbitMQ.
- `endpoint_hostname` (String) The name clients connect to (Kafka's bootstrap name); null until it resolves. It stays the same through node replacements, growth and upgrades.
- `endpoint_plaintext_port` (Number) The port without TLS (Kafka 9092, RabbitMQ 5672) while plaintext_port is true; null otherwise.
- `endpoint_port` (Number) The TLS port: Kafka 9093 (SASL_SSL), RabbitMQ 5671 (AMQPS).
- `endpoint_unauthenticated_port` (Number) Kafka's port without client authentication, 9091, while unauthenticated_access is enabled; null otherwise.
- `id` (String) Cluster ID (hqc_).
- `operation_id` (String) Most recent operation initiated by this resource; unavailable on import.
- `organization_id` (String) Organization managed by the configured provider.
- `resource_name` (String) IAM resource name.
- `status` (String) What the cluster is doing.
- `vpc_id` (String) VPC of the subnet.

<a id="nestedatt--settings"></a>
### Nested Schema for `settings`

Optional:

- `auto_create_topics` (Boolean) Whether a topic a client names is created with the cluster's defaults (true when left out at create).
- `default_partitions` (Number) Partitions of an auto-created topic, 1 to 100 (1 when left out at create).
- `default_retention_ms` (Number) How long a topic keeps messages unless it says otherwise: -1 keeps them, else 60000 to a year (a week when left out at create).


<a id="nestedatt--unauthenticated_access"></a>
### Nested Schema for `unauthenticated_access`

Optional:

- `access` (String) readWrite or readOnly (readOnly when left out at create).
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the listener is on (false when left out at create).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Replace identifiers with values from your organization.
terraform import ezghcloud_hosted_queue_cluster.example 'ORGANIZATION_ID/PROJECT_ID/CLUSTER_ID'
```
